name: products
title: Products
description: Sellable items: physical goods, digital downloads, services, subscriptions, and depreciable assets share this one schema via product_type. Locations and stock_moves (derived stock levels) now live alongside this schema in the same package -- see schemas/locations.json, schemas/stock_moves.json, and object_stock.py. Orders and order lines are a separate package (app-orders); this schema's product_id is what their order_lines optionally relate to. price_cents/cost_cents/salvage_value_cents are integer cents, never a float or currency type. v4 is merchandising, and its one load-bearing decision is that A VARIANT IS A PRODUCT: a size/colour configuration gets its own row here -- own SKU, own price, own stock level -- with parent_product_id naming the row it displays under and options saying what it is. Stock moves, pricing, checkout, fulfillment and the books all key on product_id TODAY, so variants-as-products means every one of those keeps working with ZERO changes, and 'how many medium navy totes are left?' is the same question as any other stock question, answered by the same fold. The alternative -- a variants table hanging under one product -- is the model that gives every integration a products-vs-variants split personality, two ids for one sellable thing, and a stock report that cannot answer the question anybody actually asks. category is one flat text field and deliberately not a taxonomy tree; image_file_id is a POINTER into the owner's files (served by the existing /api/files/{id} endpoint), never bytes in the catalogue. v5 is the commerce money layer's half of the catalogue, and it is four fields and no new machinery. is_gift_card marks a product that sells STORED VALUE rather than a thing -- an ordinary sale whose fulfilment credits a wallet (app-billing) instead of putting something in a box. backorder_policy decides what checkout does when the shelf is empty, defaulting to refuse, which is exactly today's behaviour: a catalogue that has never heard of the field behaves identically, and nothing starts selling stock it does not have because a column was missing. reorder_point and reorder_quantity feed a nightly fold that writes a SUGGESTION, never a purchase order -- a machine that raises POs on its own is how a business orders forty pallets of the wrong thing.

fields.name: product_type
fields.label: Type
fields.help: Matches the predecessor system's Product model type choices (reconciled against a private source audit, not part of this repo). asset carries the depreciation fields below; behavior (a monthly depreciation schedule) is not built here, only the fields.

fields.name: is_gift_card
fields.label: Gift Card
fields.help: This product SELLS STORED VALUE rather than a thing. It is an ordinary sale in every other respect -- it has a price, it goes in a basket, it is invoiced and paid for -- and its fulfilment is app-billing's system_gift_card_issue opening a wallet with a bearer code and crediting it with the line total, instead of a picker putting something in a box. Deliberately a flag rather than a sixth product_type: a gift card can be physical (a card in an envelope) or digital (a code in an email), and folding it into the type enum would make every place that asks 'does this sit on a shelf?' -- checkout's stock gate, the pick list, the books -- learn a new answer. The face value is the LINE TOTAL, so three at $25 is three $25 cards; a shop wanting 'pay $45, get $50' needs a face-value field this deliberately does not invent.

fields.name: category
fields.label: Category
fields.help: One flat name -- "Mugs", "Prints", "Workshops" -- and deliberately NOT a taxonomy tree. A tree is what a store builds because a platform offers one and then fights forever over which branch a thing belongs on; a small business has eight categories and already knows what they are called. The shop page groups on this exact string, so two spellings really are two categories: that is the price of a field anybody can fill in without asking permission, and it is cheaper than the argument. Blank is fine and is not an error -- an uncategorised product still sells, it just lands under "Everything else" at the bottom of the page. If a real catalogue ever outgrows flat, tags already exist as a system.

fields.name: parent_product_id
fields.label: Variant Of
fields.help: The product this one displays under -- DISPLAY GROUPING ONLY, and nothing else. It does not change how this row is sold, counted, picked or booked: the variant has its own SKU, its own price_cents and its own stock level, and every system in the building still keys on product_id exactly as it did. That is the whole point (see this schema's description): the shop page collapses children under the parent card and the product page offers a picker, and no other code learns a new noun. Blank for the ordinary case, which is most products.

fields.name: options
fields.label: Options
fields.help: What this variant IS, as a small JSON object: {"size": "M", "colour": "navy"}. Text and not a typed field because the option NAMES are the seller's vocabulary -- size, colour, grind, length, finish -- and a schema that enumerated them would be a schema every seller has to fight before they can list a product. Key order is the seller's order and the shop renders it in that order, so "size" first reads the way a label is written. Unparseable JSON renders as nothing rather than as an error: a mistyped brace must not take a product off the shelf.

fields.name: image_file_id
fields.label: Image
fields.help: The file id of the product photograph in the owner's files, served by the endpoint that already exists at /api/files/{id}. The catalogue stores a POINTER and never bytes -- same posture as digital_file_id, and the reason a product row stays a row. Mark that file public (files.is_public) or a shopper who is not signed in gets nothing back. Blank renders a neutral placeholder block on the shop page rather than a broken image: a text-only shop is not a shop, but a broken-image icon is worse than an honest blank.

fields.name: backorder_policy
fields.label: When Out Of Stock
fields.help: What checkout does when the shelf is empty. refuse is the DEFAULT and is exactly today's behaviour, which is the whole safety of this field: a catalogue written before it existed, or a value typed wrong, or a product somebody imported all behave as the shop behaved yesterday, and nothing starts selling stock it does not have because a column was missing. allow takes the order anyway and marks the line backordered -- real stores sell the incoming shipment, and a hard refusal on every empty shelf is a shop turning away money it could take -- and the goods ship when stock exists, never before. notify still refuses, but RECORDS THE INTEREST (a backorders row) so somebody can be told when it is back: refusing while remembering beats refusing and forgetting, which loses the customer twice.

fields.name: reorder_point
fields.label: Reorder At
fields.help: The level at or below which somebody should think about buying more. 0 means off, and off is the default: a reorder point nobody chose is a number that makes a queue lie. system_reorder_check folds stock levels nightly and writes a SUGGESTION when on-hand reaches this -- at or below, not merely below, because 'reorder at 5' means five is already the moment, and a shop that has to hit four has been told the wrong number.

fields.name: reorder_quantity
fields.label: Reorder Quantity
fields.help: How many to suggest buying. 0 means the suggestion carries no quantity and simply says the shelf is low, which is honest: how much to buy depends on lead time, case size and what the supplier will sell, and a machine that guessed would be guessing about somebody's money.

fields.name: income_account
fields.label: Income Account
fields.help: The real predecessor links to a finance Account (income side). No finance package exists yet in this codebase -- carried as a plain text account id so a future app-finance package has somewhere to point without a backfill.

fields.name: expense_account
fields.label: Expense Account
fields.help: Same provenance as income_account, expense side.

fields.name: digital_file_id
fields.label: Digital File
fields.help: Pointer to the downloadable file for a digital product. No enforced relation to app-files yet (this package has no dependency on it) -- carried as a plain text id so a future digital-delivery slice has somewhere to point without a backfill.

fields.name: useful_life_months
fields.label: Useful Life (months)
fields.help: ASSET parity field, carried from the predecessor system's depreciation fields (reconciled against a private source audit, not part of this repo). Only meaningful when product_type is asset; depreciation math itself is not built here.

fields.name: salvage_value_cents
fields.label: Salvage Value (cents)
fields.help: ASSET parity field. Integer cents, same doctrine as price_cents/cost_cents.

fields.name: depreciation_method
fields.label: Depreciation Method
fields.help: ASSET parity field. No default -- blank means not an asset, or an asset whose method has not been set yet; left unset rather than forced to a guessed default.

fields.name: asset_status
fields.label: Asset Status
fields.help: ASSET parity field. Kept as plain text (not an enum) in v1: the predecessor's asset disposal states are a later slice's concern, not reconstructed here.

fields.name: entity_id
fields.label: Entity
fields.help: The set of books this belongs to (65 multi-entity). Optional during rollout; backfilled to the owner's default entity, set by the entity switcher on new writes.
